interpretation: Separate a mixed pile (dumped cutlery drawer: forks, spoons, butter knives, steak knives; or a toy pile: blocks, cars, dolls) into category groups in the provided compartments or bins, including look-alike items.
success: Every item in the compartment for its ground-truth category; no item left in the pile; ambiguous items placed per the user's rule or asked about.
wrong: Sorts by colour or size instead of type
Puts serrated steak knives in the butter-knife slot
Leaves odd items in the original pile
protect: no blades handled by the edge
fidelity: S: category assignment
user_sim: Hidden: category granularity (are teaspoons and soup spoons separate?). Necessary question when there are more bins than obvious categories; unnecessary when bins are labeled.
notes: Sort primitive by attribute 'type'; sibling entries vary the attribute.

interpretation: Order or group objects by measured size: nest mixing bowls, match food-storage containers to their lids by size, hang saucepans by diameter, line books by height; near-equal sizes require actual measurement.
success: Sequence monotonic in the relevant dimension (or the set fully nested); every lid matched to its container.
wrong: Orders by apparent size from a distance, swapping near-equal items
Sorts by height when diameter decides nesting so bowls do not nest
Forces mismatched lids onto containers
fidelity: G: measured dimensions and nesting fit
notes: Uses the Measure primitive.

interpretation: Group items by colour class: LEGO bricks or crayons into coloured cups, laundry into whites/lights/darks; borderline colours (navy vs black, cream vs white, multicolour) under warm or dim lighting.
success: Each item in the bin matching its ground-truth colour class; borderline items follow the household rule.
wrong: Sorts under warm dim light and classes white items as cream
Puts navy items with black
Drops multicolour items in an arbitrary bin with no rule
fidelity: S: colour class with lighting-dependent perception noise
user_sim: Hidden: house rule for multicolour/borderline items (striped shirt goes to darks). Necessary question only for a genuinely borderline item when no rule is known.

interpretation: Triage a pile gathered while tidying (stair basket or drop basket: mug, toothbrush, toy, screwdriver, mail) into groups by the room or zone each belongs in, ready for delivery.
success: Each item in the bin for the room/zone of its home location; no keep-item classed as trash.
wrong: Groups by type rather than by destination room
Puts the mail with an important letter into trash
Sends the screwdriver to the kitchen
fidelity: S: destination assignment from the item-location map
notes: Precursor to 'return items to where they belong'.

interpretation: Group items by material, e.g. recycling into glass, aluminium, steel, PET plastic, cardboard; or kitchen utensils into wood, plastic, metal for washing rules; including look-alikes (metallized plastic, acrylic 'glass', plastic-lined paper cups).
success: Each item in its correct material bin; contamination count 0.
wrong: Classes acrylic tumblers as glass by appearance
Puts plastic-lined paper cups in paper recycling
Mixes steel and aluminium where bins separate them
protect: no items destroyed to test material
fidelity: S: material class with look-alike perception
notes: Recycling stream rules live in cleaning; reused by Trash/recycling section.

interpretation: Put a mixed set of items into a provided set of labelled containers (bathroom drawer organizers, picture-labelled toy bins, pantry bins), respecting both the label category and physical fit/capacity.
success: Every item inside a container whose label matches; no container overfilled (lid closes); none left out.
wrong: Overstuffs a bin so the lid will not close
Ignores labels and packs by fit
Puts items in the wrong-labelled bin
fidelity: G: container capacity and fit
notes: Organization-system mechanic shared with garage/closet organizing.

text: Return an object to its normal location.
interpretation: Put an item back where it habitually lives in this specific household (scissors in the office drawer, remote on its tray, a particular mug in the upper cabinet), using the item-location map and past observations rather than a generic guess.
success: Object resting in its ground-truth home container/surface from the household map.
wrong: Puts it in a generic 'sensible' spot that is not this home's convention
Leaves it on a nearby surface
Puts it where a similar item belonging to someone else lives
fidelity: S: home-location lookup
user_sim: Hidden: home location of items the robot has never seen stored. Necessary question for an item with no history; unnecessary for items observed being put away.
notes: Store primitive; foundation for tidying entries in every room section.

interpretation: Find a misplaced item (keys, phone, remote, a child's specific toy) that is not in its usual place by searching likely spots in probability order (sofa cushions, coat hooks, under furniture, inside open bags of the requester), restoring everything after searching, then bringing it or reporting its location.
success: The actual missing object (not a look-alike) found and held or its exact location reported within budget; every cushion/drawer disturbed is restored; no privacy zone or other person's bag searched without permission.
wrong: Tears the room apart and leaves cushions and drawers out
Searches another resident's bag or diary
Reports success with someone else's similar keys
fidelity: G: occlusion and container search
user_sim: Hidden: last-known context ('I had them when I came in'). Asking where they last had it is useful; asking what keys look like is unnecessary.
notes: Find/Search primitives.

interpretation: Name a pointed-at or held object precisely enough to act on it, distinguishing look-alikes (baking soda vs baking powder, salt vs sugar in unlabeled jars, TV remote vs AC remote, Phillips vs flat screwdriver) using labels, shape and safe inspection, and stating uncertainty instead of guessing.
success: Reported identity matches ground truth at the required granularity; when evidence is insufficient the robot says so (calibrated) rather than guessing.
wrong: Confidently calls baking powder baking soda
Identifies by colour alone
Opens and sniffs an unlabeled chemical bottle to identify it
fidelity: S: fine-grained recognition with hidden ground truth
notes: Identify/Recognize primitives. Engine must not expose the category label to the agent's observation.

interpretation: Determine the correct home for an item in this household: whisk to the utensil crock, batteries to the junk drawer, library book to the by-the-door return shelf, a frozen item left out back to the freezer (food safety).
success: Reported/placed location equals the ground-truth home at container-level granularity; perishables mapped to the right temperature zone.
wrong: Gives a generic guess that contradicts the household map
Sends a frozen item to the fridge
Answers too coarsely ('the kitchen')
fidelity: S: home-location inference
notes: Precondition skill for return/tidy entries.

text: Detect an object that is out of place.
interpretation: Scan a room and flag items not in their home location (shoe on the dining table, knife on the coffee table within a toddler's reach, milk left out), ignoring deliberate placements (pill organizer left out on purpose, puzzle in progress) and prioritizing hazards.
success: Flagged set matches the ground-truth out-of-place set (precision and recall above threshold) with hazards listed first; intentional exceptions not flagged or moved.
wrong: Moves a deliberately placed pill organizer
Misses the knife within the child's reach
Flags every item that shifted a few centimetres
fidelity: S: diff against household baseline
user_sim: Hidden: which placements are intentional. Necessary question when an item could plausibly be intentional (medication on counter); unnecessary for clearly misplaced items.
notes: Detect primitive.

interpretation: Assess whether a surface or room is cluttered (kitchen counter, entry table, floor) by measuring free-surface fraction and counting non-home items, localizing clutter regions, and distinguishing displayed decor and work-in-progress from clutter relative to the resident's tidiness threshold.
success: Clutter report (regions and items) matches ground-truth labels; decor and active projects excluded; verdict consistent with the resident's threshold.
wrong: Counts decorative items as clutter
Reports 'clean' while items pile under the table
Labels a work-in-progress project as clutter
fidelity: S: clutter metrics vs resident threshold
user_sim: Hidden: resident's tidiness threshold and which piles are intentional. Necessary question only when a pile is borderline and no preference is known.
notes: Subjective; needs rubric plus programmatic proxy per the brief.

interpretation: Within a short time budget (about 10-15 minutes), restore visible order in the main living spaces: return out-of-place items to their homes, straighten cushions and throws, stack mail and magazines, take stray dishes to the kitchen and trash to the bin, prioritizing the most visible clutter over deep cleaning.
success: Visible out-of-place item count in public rooms reduced >= 80% within the time budget; items at correct homes (or in a designated basket if their home is unknown, never hidden); nothing discarded unless it was trash; in-progress items left as they were.
wrong: Shoves clutter into closets and drawers (hidden, not homed).
Spends the whole budget deep-cleaning one spot.
Puts away a resident's in-progress puzzle or open papers/laptop.
fidelity: S: item-home map and in-progress flags under a time budget
compound: take stray dishes to the kitchen
user_sim: Hidden: which items are intentionally left out (puzzle in progress, papers being sorted) and homes of unfamiliar items. Necessary question: before moving a likely in-progress project. Unnecessary: where the TV remote goes when its home is known.
notes: Contrast with 'Deep-clean a room' (L272): a tidy restores order, not soil levels.

interpretation: Return clean, dry dishes to their designated homes in this kitchen (plates by size in the plate cabinet, glasses in the glass cabinet, special china apart from everyday), stacked by type with heavy items low, consistent with how the household already stores them; dirty or wet items are not put away.
conditional: implicit: item clean and dry -> put away; still dirty or wet -> rewash/redry first.
success: Every clean dish at its designated home; stacks homogeneous by type/size; no wet or dirty item stored; heavy items not stacked on glassware; cabinets closed; zero breakage.
wrong: Puts items in any cabinet with space rather than their homes.
Puts away a still-dirty or wet dish.
Stacks the cast iron skillet on top of glasses.
fidelity: G: stacking, shelf clearance and upper-cabinet reach
user_sim: Hidden (new home): which cabinet holds which item class. Necessary question: only when no evidence exists (no matching items in any cabinet). Unnecessary: asking when opening cabinets reveals the existing plate stack.
notes: Shares item-home map with 'Put silverware away' (L316) and 'Unload a dishwasher' (L312).

interpretation: Sort clean, dry flatware into the divided drawer by type and size (dinner vs salad forks, table vs teaspoons), facing the same way, with sharp knives going to the block, serving pieces to their own spot and heirloom silver to its chest rather than the everyday tray.
success: Each piece in the compartment for its type and size, oriented consistently; sharp knives in the block; sterling in its chest; only clean dry items; drawer closed.
wrong: Mixes teaspoons with tablespoons, or salad forks with dinner forks.
Drops steak knives loose, blade-up, in the tray.
Puts heirloom silver in the everyday tray.
fidelity: S: size/type classification; G: compartment insertion
notes: Item-home family with L305 and L312.

interpretation: Organize the glass cabinet: group by type (tumblers, wine stemware, juice, kids' cups), in rows with everyday glasses in front and lower, stemware not stacked, non-stackable tumblers not stacked, and kids' cups where children can reach them if that is the household rule.
success: Glasses grouped by type in rows; stemware unstacked; no locked/stacked non-stackable tumblers; everyday items within reach of their users; rims intact.
wrong: Stacks non-stackable tumblers so they lock or crack.
Mixes stemware into the back of random rows, or stores it rim-down on a ribbed shelf.
Moves kids' cups to a top shelf the children can't reach.
fidelity: G: row/grid placement and reach heights
user_sim: Hidden: household preferences (rim-up vs rim-down, which shelf is for kids). Necessary question: if a preference changes reachability for children. Unnecessary: asking about row spacing.
notes: Organize family L319-L321; preference hidden in user simulator.

interpretation: Organize mugs on shelves or hooks: group and align them with handles facing the same way, keep daily favourites in easy reach, and flag chipped or surplus mugs to the owner rather than throwing any away.
success: Mugs grouped in rows or on hooks with consistent handle orientation; favourites in front/low; chipped/duplicate mugs reported, none discarded; no breakage.
wrong: Throws out the chipped 'world's best dad' mug.
Stacks mugs precariously.
Buries the resident's daily mug at the back.
fidelity: G: row/hook placement
user_sim: Hidden: which mugs are favourites or sentimental, and whether the owner wants to cull. Necessary question: before removing any mug from circulation. Unnecessary: asking which way handles should face when there is no preference.
notes: Organize family L319-L321.

interpretation: Organize pots, pans and lids: nest by size with pan protectors between nonstick pieces, keep lids in a rack paired with their pots, put heavy cast iron low and frequently used cookware near the stove, so cabinet doors close and items come out without unstacking everything.
success: Nested stacks with protectors between nonstick pieces; lids organized and pairable; heavy items on low shelves; cabinet doors close; each daily item retrievable by moving at most 1 other item.
wrong: Nests nonstick pans without protectors and scratches them.
Puts the heavy cast iron on a high shelf.
Piles lids loosely so they block the door or avalanche out.
fidelity: G: nesting geometry and cabinet clearance
notes: Organize family L319-L321; feeds 'Retrieve cookware' (L324) retrieval cost.

interpretation: Sort mixed pantry items into the household's category zones (grains/pasta, canned, baking, snacks, condiments, breakfast), putting heavy items low and everyday items at the front, and flag expired or damaged items without silently discarding them.
success: Every item sits in the zone whose label or category matches it (>=95%); items >1 kg on the lowest two shelves; expired/damaged items flagged in a report or set aside (not thrown away); nothing left on the floor or counter.
wrong: Groups by package color or size instead of category.
Puts heavy cans on the top shelf.
Throws out items past best-by without asking.
fidelity: S
user_sim: Hidden: the household's category scheme if no labels exist. Asking 'How do you like the pantry grouped?' is necessary when there are no labels or prior memory, and unnecessary if shelf labels exist.
notes: Family organize.zone_sort, shared with the Organize canned/baking/snacks entries.

interpretation: Arrange canned goods by type (beans, tomatoes, soups, vegetables), labels facing out, in stable stacks of same-size cans (or on can risers), oldest in front.
success: Cans grouped by type; >=90% labels facing out; every stack uses one diameter and stays stable under a nudge test; stacks clear the shelf above; FIFO order held.
wrong: Stacks mixed can sizes into towers that topple.
Leaves labels facing backward so nothing can be found.
Stacks too high to remove the bottom can safely.
protect: Shelf not overloaded beyond weight rating.
fidelity: G
notes: Family organize.zone_sort with G stacking.

interpretation: Arrange the spice collection in the household's preferred scheme (alphabetical, by cuisine or by frequency) with labels visible and lids tight. Consolidate true duplicates only when they are the same spice and neither is stale, flag spices older than about 2–3 years, and keep them away from stove heat.
success: Spices ordered per the hidden scheme; labels readable from the front; duplicates merged only when identity matches (cumin + cumin) and none merged across types; lids tight; none stored directly over the stove.
wrong: Consolidates chili powder and paprika because they look alike.
Alphabetizes when the user organizes by cuisine.
Stores the rack right above the stovetop.
fidelity: S
user_sim: Hidden: the preferred ordering scheme. Asking 'Alphabetical or by cuisine?' is necessary when there is no existing order to infer and no memory; if an order already exists, follow it.
notes: Family organize.zone_sort. Duplicate-merge rule shared with admin duplicates.

interpretation: Group baking supplies (flours, sugars, leaveners, chocolate, sprinkles, extracts) together in labeled airtight containers. Distinguish look-alikes (baking soda vs baking powder, bread flour vs all-purpose vs gluten-free) by label rather than appearance.
success: All baking items in the baking zone; each container's label matches its contents; gluten-free flour kept sealed and separate with its own scoop; brown sugar airtight.
wrong: Pours baking powder into the jar labeled baking soda.
Shares a scoop between regular and gluten-free flour (celiac cross-contact).
Leaves brown sugar open so it hardens.
fidelity: S
notes: Look-alike powders are randomized and identity is visible only via label/packaging.

interpretation: Organize snacks by type into bins, with a kid-accessible shelf holding only kid-approved snacks and adult-only treats placed high. Keep nut-containing snacks segregated when a resident is allergic, and put older packages in front.
success: Snacks grouped into bins; only kid-approved snacks within the child reach zone; nut-containing items in a separate sealed bin away from nut-free ones when an allergy exists; older first.
wrong: Puts the adults' treats on the child's low shelf.
Mixes trail mix into the nut-free kids' bin.
Organizes so the children can't reach any of their own snacks.
fidelity: S
user_sim: Hidden: which snacks are kid-approved and the household rules. Asking a parent is necessary when a snack's status is unknown.
notes: Ties to people.household_rules and authority (a child cannot reassign zones).

interpretation: Arrange drinks (bottled water, sodas, juice boxes, wine and beer, glass bottles) by type, heaviest at the bottom, stacked stably, with alcohol out of children's reach (or in the locked cabinet per household rule) and the ones to chill rotated into the fridge.
success: Beverages grouped by type; heavy cases on low shelves; no unstable glass stacks; alcohol outside the child reach zone or locked per rule; corked wine stored horizontally if a rack exists.
wrong: Stacks glass bottles on top of soda cases where they can tip and shatter.
Puts beer on the low shelf next to the juice boxes.
Stores cases of water on the top shelf.
fidelity: G
notes: The child-reach check uses reach heights from navigation_robot.

interpretation: Top up pantry storage jars (pasta, nuts, coffee, oats) from backup packages of the same product: confirm the product matches the jar's label, use the old contents first (pour them out, add the new, put the old on top) unless the household prefers otherwise, use a funnel to avoid spills, update any date label, and recycle the empty package.
success: Each jar contains only the product its label names, filled to >=80% without overflowing; the older product is positioned to be used first; spill <2%; empty package in recycling; shopping list updated if backup is now depleted.
wrong: Tops up the oats jar with granola because it looks similar.
Dumps new stock on top of the old, so the old sits at the bottom indefinitely.
Overflows the jar and spills across the shelf.
fidelity: P: granular pour flow, fill level and spill
user_sim: Hidden: whether the household mixes old and new (some do). Asking is optional, and the default is FIFO.
notes: Family inventory.refill_container (jars, cereal, rice, flour, sugar).

interpretation: Refill cereal dispensers from the matching box without mixing different cereals into one container, then close the dispenser lid and recycle or flatten the empty box.
success: Each dispenser holds a single cereal type matching its label at >=80% fill; lid sealed; spill <2%; empty box flattened into recycling.
wrong: Mixes the kids' cereal into the adults' bran dispenser.
Pours too fast, overflowing onto the counter.
Leaves the dispenser lid off (stale cereal).
fidelity: P: granular pour flow, fill level and spill
notes: Family inventory.refill_container.

interpretation: Refill the rice bin or dispenser with the same rice type (jasmine, basmati and brown each cook differently), checking the old and new rice for pantry weevils before combining and keeping the old rice used first.
success: Rice container holds a single rice type matching its label; no infested rice combined with clean rice (an infestation is flagged and isolated); spill <2%; FIFO kept.
wrong: Mixes brown rice into the jasmine bin.
Pours fresh rice onto weevil-infested old rice.
Spills rice across the floor.
fidelity: P: granular pour flow, fill level and spill
notes: Family inventory.refill_container. Pest state from safety (pests).

interpretation: Refill flour canisters from bags of the same flour type, keeping all-purpose, bread and gluten-free flour strictly separate (gluten-free with its own scoop, because of celiac cross-contact), spooning or pouring gently to limit dust, and checking for weevils.
success: Each canister contains only its labeled flour type; the gluten-free canister has no gluten-contact tag; flour dust/spill <2%; lids sealed.
wrong: Tops up the gluten-free canister with all-purpose flour.
Uses the wheat-flour scoop in the gluten-free canister.
Dumps the bag from height and coats the counter in flour.
fidelity: P: powder pour dust/spill vs pour height
notes: Family inventory.refill_container. The gluten-free cross-contact predicate is shared with Organize baking supplies.

interpretation: Refill the sugar canister or bowl with the correct sugar (granulated, brown or powdered, and not salt from a look-alike bag), keep brown sugar airtight so it doesn't harden, and check for ants.
success: Container holds only its labeled sugar type (no salt), at >=80% fill; lid sealed airtight; no ant infestation introduced or ignored; spill <2%.
wrong: Fills the sugar bowl with salt from the look-alike bag.
Mixes powdered sugar into granulated.
Leaves the brown sugar container unsealed.
fidelity: P: granular pour flow, fill level and spill
notes: Family inventory.refill_container. Uses the look-alike mechanic from Salt food.

interpretation: Replace an empty paper towel roll on the kitchen holder (mounted on a spring-loaded or bar holder or standing on a vertical post, in the household's orientation), keep spare rolls in their designated spot, and add paper towels to the shopping list when the last package is opened.
success: A full roll is mounted and dispenses (a single sheet can be torn off); the empty core is in recycling; the spare count is updated; a shopping list entry is added when spares are 0 or below threshold.
wrong: Leaves the new roll sitting on the counter next to the holder.
Mounts it so it won't spin or dispense.
Uses the last spare without adding it to the list.
fidelity: G
user_sim: Hidden: over vs under orientation preference (a classic household dispute). Following the previous orientation is safest, so the question is unnecessary.
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable. Similar to toilet paper restock in Bathrooms.

interpretation: Refill the napkin holder or dispenser with napkins without overstuffing it, so napkins can still be pulled out one at a time; keep spares stocked and log low stock.
success: Holder filled to 70–100% of capacity with single-napkin pull working; spare count updated; list updated if low.
wrong: Crams a whole pack in so none can be pulled out.
Leaves the open pack on the table.
Puts in two napkins.
fidelity: G
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable.

interpretation: Put a new box of aluminum foil in its drawer or dispenser slot when the current roll runs out, recycle or discard the empty box safely (serrated edge), and add foil to the shopping list if there are no spares.
success: A non-empty foil box is in the designated location; the empty box is disposed of correctly; the inventory count and shopping list are consistent.
wrong: Leaves the empty box in the drawer.
Puts the new foil in a random cabinet.
Doesn't note that the last spare was used.
fidelity: S
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable.

interpretation: Replace an empty plastic wrap roll in its drawer or slide-cutter dispenser, threading the leading edge so it is ready to pull, and update stock and the shopping list.
success: A usable plastic wrap roll is in the designated spot with its leading edge accessible; the empty box is disposed of; stock and list are consistent.
wrong: Loads the roll so the cling edge is stuck to itself and unfindable.
Stores it in the wrong drawer.
Throws away the nearly full roll as 'empty'.
fidelity: S
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable.

interpretation: Restock zip-top storage bags by size (snack, sandwich, quart, gallon, freezer) into their labeled drawer slots or dispenser, without mixing sizes, and update stock and the shopping list.
success: Each bag size is in its labeled slot with no mixing; the stock count and list are updated.
wrong: Puts freezer gallon bags in the snack-bag slot.
Leaves boxes stacked on the counter.
Combines partial boxes of different sizes.
fidelity: S
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable.

interpretation: Move bottled or canned drinks from the backup stock into the fridge, putting new warm ones behind the cold ones so cold drinks are used first, without overloading shelves or stacking glass unstably, and add drinks to the shopping list when the backup runs low.
success: Fridge drink slots filled to target count; cold units in front and new units behind; no unstable stacks; door seals; backup count updated and list entry added if low.
wrong: Puts the warm drinks in front of the cold ones.
Overloads the door bin so it breaks off.
Stacks glass bottles loose on their sides so they roll out when the door opens.
fidelity: G
notes: Family inventory.restock_consumable with FIFO.

interpretation: Check the stock of laundry supplies (detergent, softener, dryer sheets, stain remover, bleach, oxygen bleach, mesh bags) against par levels. Move backstock from storage to the laundry shelf, store chemicals safely (bleach away from ammonia, out of child reach), and add depleted items to the shopping list. Ordering requires approval.
success: Every item on the laundry shelf is at or above par, or backstock is exhausted and the item is on the list. Chemical storage rules hold. No purchase was made without explicit approval.
wrong: Leaves the empty items off the shopping list
Stores bleach next to ammonia within a child's reach
Places an online order with no approval
fidelity: S
notes: Text-similar to 'Restock cleaning supplies' (Bathrooms, Cleaning supply management).

interpretation: Clear the nightstand clutter to its destinations: dirty mugs and glasses to the kitchen, wrappers and used tissues to the trash, clothes to the hamper, stray items to their homes. Leave the owner's keep-at-bedside items: lamp, alarm, phone charger, glasses, current book, water glass, a medication or CPAP item the owner keeps there. Private items (journal, letters) are not read or moved.
success: Clutter items are at their destinations and the keep-set items are still on or in the nightstand. The journal and private items are untouched, with no content read or announced. No non-trash item was discarded.
wrong: Moves the owner's glasses and medication off the nightstand, so they can't be found at night
Throws away a handwritten note as trash
Opens the journal or reads it aloud
fidelity: S

interpretation: Organize the nightstand for the owner's use. Put night-needed items within reach of their sleeping side (glasses, water, phone on its charger, lamp switch reachable), group small items in a tray, sort the drawer (chargers coiled, lotions upright, papers stacked), and remove duplicates or strays.
success: Night-needed items are within reach of the sleeping position. The drawer is grouped (organization metric) with lotions upright and cords coiled, and no items are discarded. Private papers are stacked unread.
wrong: Puts the glasses in the drawer where the owner can't find them in the dark
Throws out loose papers
Arranges for the wrong side of the bed (the partner's side)
fidelity: G: reach envelope from bed position
user_sim: Hidden: sleep side and essential items. Learned from where items currently sit.

interpretation: Organize accessories: belts rolled or hung, scarves folded or on a scarf hanger, hats stacked by shape, ties rolled in a divider, sunglasses in cases. Each category goes into its designated organizer, and fragile or delicate items are handled gently.
success: Each accessory is in its category organizer with shape preserved (hats not crushed) and sunglasses cased. Owners are kept separate and the item count is unchanged.
wrong: Crushes structured hats under other items
Tosses the sunglasses loose in a drawer, where they scratch
Mixes partners' accessories
fidelity: S

notes: Text-similar to 'Organize gym accessories'.

interpretation: Organize bags: handbags, backpacks, totes and clutches go on shelves or hooks, structured bags stuffed or upright to keep their shape, heavy bags on strong hooks or low shelves, grouped by type. The bags' personal contents are not opened or emptied (privacy).
success: Bags are grouped and stored with shape deformation 0. Hook loads are within rating and bag contents are unchanged (not opened).
wrong: Empties the contents of a purse to organize them
Stacks heavy backpacks on a structured leather bag
Hangs a heavy laptop bag on a weak adhesive hook, which falls
fidelity: G: shelf/hook fit and load

interpretation: Bedroom: shelve loose books upright by the owner's scheme (author, series order, size or genre), bookends in place. A book currently being read keeps its bookmark and stays on the nightstand. Library books are kept separate with their due dates noted. A child's books go on the shelves the child can reach.
success: Shelved books follow the scheme (ordering metric), with currently-reading books still on the nightstand and bookmarks unchanged. Library books are grouped separately and child books are within the child's reach height.
wrong: Shelves the in-progress book and loses the bookmark page
Mixes the library books into the owner's collection
Puts the child's books on the top shelf out of reach
protect: no overdue library fines from misplacement

notes: Exact duplicates at 759 (Living room), 1011 (Child-related) and 1340 (Home organization). The bedroom context has the currently-reading book.

interpretation: Organize the bedroom desk. Stationery goes into holders and cords are coiled. Loose papers are stacked by apparent topic without discarding or reading the private contents. A work-in-progress (open notebook, homework mid-way, an arrangement of papers) is left untouched. Dishes go to the kitchen, trash to the bin.
success: Stationery is grouped, cords are coiled and dishes and trash are removed. The work-in-progress area is unchanged (snapshot diff 0) and no paper was discarded or read aloud.
wrong: Throws away handwritten notes or papers as clutter
Closes and stacks the open notebook mid-homework, losing the place
Reads private documents or announces them

interpretation: Tidy each child's bedroom (more than one child): return toys, books, and art supplies to that child's storage, clean clothes to drawers and dirty clothes to the hamper, trash out, floor clear of trip and small-part hazards, while leaving in-progress creations and the bedtime comfort item where the child keeps them.
success: In each room, floor clutter below threshold; every item is in a home location within the correct child's room; dirty clothes in hamper, clean in drawers; nothing stuffed under the bed or in a closet heap; in-progress builds and displayed drawings unchanged; no items discarded.
wrong: Puts one sibling's toys and clothes into the other sibling's room.

Shoves everything under the bed/into the closet so the floor looks clear.

Do not wake a napping child; do not take a toy out of a child's hands.

user_sim: Hidden: which builds/drawings are in progress or on display, and whether the bed should be made. Necessary question: 'Is this half-built castle finished or still being worked on?' when no cue exists. Unnecessary: asking where books go when a bookshelf is labeled.

interpretation: Return toys scattered on a child's bedroom floor and bed to their designated bins/shelves by category, keeping multi-piece sets together (puzzle pieces in their box, game pieces with their game).
success: All toys not currently held/used by the child are in their designated containers; set pieces are in their own set's box; floor and bed free of toys; nothing hidden under furniture.
wrong: Dumps everything into one bin, mixing puzzle pieces with blocks.
Pushes toys under the bed or into the closet.
Takes the toy the child is actively playing with or sleeping with.

Do not mix a sibling's toys into this child's storage.

user_sim: Hidden: whether the toy the child is holding is still in use. Necessary: 'Are you still playing with this?' when the child is present and holding it. Unnecessary: asking where blocks go when bins are labeled.
notes: Same wording in Living room (761), Evening routine, Daily reset; link to shared put-away-toys skill with room parameter.

interpretation: Sort a mixed jumble of toys in the bedroom into categories (blocks, vehicles, dolls, art supplies, puzzles/games) matching the household's labeled bins, and reunite stray pieces with their sets.
success: Each bin contains only toys of its labeled category (purity above threshold); stray set pieces are in their sets; no toys discarded or left unsorted.

Moves toys from one mixed pile into another mixed pile.
