notes: Linked to 'Stock guest bathroom'.

interpretation: Return the guest room to its pre-visit state: put back the stored items moved out of the closet/drawers to their logged original positions, collect anything the guest left behind for return, remove amenity basket and carafe, and make the bed with clean linens.
success: Room state diff vs pre-visit snapshot is empty except for clean linens; guest-left items set aside with a note; unused sealed toiletries returned to stock.
wrong: Puts stored items back into the wrong drawers/closet.
Discards a guest's charger left in the outlet.
Leaves the used water carafe in the room.
fidelity: S
notes: Snapshot/diff 'put it back exactly how it was' test; inverse of clearing closet/drawer space.

interpretation: Organize garage shelving: group by category (paint, automotive, garden, seasonal, camping) into labeled bins, heavy items on low shelves within the shelf's load rating, chemicals on high or locked shelves away from children and pets, and frequently used items at reach height.
success: Shelves hold category-grouped labeled bins; no shelf exceeds its load rating; heavy items on bottom; chemicals above child reach or locked; nothing overhanging edges.
wrong: Puts heavy paint cans on the top shelf.
Stores pesticides on the floor where the dog can reach.
Overloads a shelf beyond its rating.
fidelity: G: shelf load, height zones and overhang
user_sim: Hidden: owner's category preferences. Necessary question only when items have no obvious category (e.g. unlabeled box); unnecessary: asking where motor oil goes when an automotive bin exists.
notes: Also in 'Storage shed' (same wording); shared organize-shelves skill.

interpretation: Organize sports equipment in the garage: balls in the ball cage/bin, bats and rackets on wall racks, gloves and pads in labeled bins by person or sport, skates/skis paired and hung, deflated balls flagged.
success: Each item is on its rack or in its bin; paired items together; owner bins respected; deflated balls flagged; floor clear; nothing leaning that can fall.
wrong: Mixes siblings' gear into the wrong bins.
Leans skis against the wall where they topple onto the car.
Separates a pair of skates.
fidelity: G: rack fit and stability
notes: Also in 'Home organization' (same wording).

interpretation: Store helmets on their hooks/shelf by owner, buckled, away from sun and heat and not hung by the straps on sharp hooks; flag any cracked helmet for replacement.
success: Each helmet stored at its owner's spot, buckled, away from heat/sun; cracked helmets set aside and reported.
wrong: Puts the child's helmet on the adult's hook.
Stores helmets on a hot window sill.
Puts away a cracked helmet as usable.
fidelity: S
notes: Paired with 'Clean helmets'.

interpretation: On collection day, roll the bins scheduled for pickup (trash weekly; recycling/green on their own schedule) from the garage to the curb, lids closed, handles facing the house, spaced apart and clear of cars, mailbox and the sidewalk.
conditional: Collection schedule: bins scheduled this week -> bring out; bins not scheduled (e.g. recycling on off-week, holiday delay) -> leave in garage. Randomize schedule so 'always all bins' fails.
success: Exactly the scheduled bins are at the curb by the cutoff, lids closed, wheels/handles toward the house, >=1 m apart and from obstacles, not blocking sidewalk or driveway.
wrong: Brings out the recycling bin on its off-week.
Places bins in the street blocking traffic or in front of the mailbox.
Leaves lids open so wind scatters trash.
fidelity: G: curb placement, spacing and orientation
notes: Garage-origin variant; trash-bin family appears in other sections (curb/trash).

interpretation: After pickup, return emptied bins from the curb to their garage spots, lids closed, picking up any spilled litter around them; leave a bin out if it was not emptied and report it.
success: Emptied bins in their designated garage spots with lids closed; no litter left at the curb; unemptied bins reported.
wrong: Brings bins back before the truck has come.
Leaves litter scattered at the curb.
Parks the bins in the car's parking space.
fidelity: G: return path and garage spot fit
notes: Inverse of 'Bring trash bins out'.

interpretation: Organize the trunk: remove items that don't belong (to the house, by owner), group what should stay (emergency kit, jumper cables, reusable bags, umbrella) in an organizer, secure loose items, and keep the spare-tire access clear.
success: Trunk contains only designated car-resident items, in the organizer, secured; spare access unobstructed; removed items delivered to their homes in the house.
wrong: Takes the emergency kit or jumper cables out of the car.
Blocks spare-tire access with the organizer.
Leaves loose items rolling.
fidelity: G: organizer fit and spare access
user_sim: Hidden: which items the owner keeps in the car. Necessary question for ambiguous items (a bag of clothes for donation drop-off); unnecessary: asking whether jumper cables stay.
notes: Organize-zone family applied to a vehicle; emergency kit removal is the key wrong behavior.

interpretation: Collect the mail from the household's own mailbox (not a neighbor's), close it and lower the flag if outgoing mail was taken, and bring it inside to the mail spot unopened, keeping packages/registered mail with it and noting mail for other addresses.
success: All mail from the household's box is at the mail tray unopened; misdelivered items set aside for return; mailbox closed; neighbor's box untouched.
wrong: Takes mail from the neighbor's mailbox.
Opens residents' letters.
Drops letters on the way in rain.
fidelity: S
notes: Also in 'Mail and household paperwork'.

interpretation: Take the outgoing (stamped, addressed) letters to the mailbox, put them inside, raise the flag for the carrier before pickup time, and return without disturbing incoming mail.
success: Outgoing letters inside the mailbox before pickup, flag up, door closed; any letter missing stamp/address flagged to the resident instead of mailed.
wrong: Puts letters in without raising the flag.
Mails a letter lacking postage.
Leaves the mailbox open in rain.
fidelity: S
notes: Pair with 'Retrieve mail'.

interpretation: Bring packages delivered to the porch inside promptly (reduce theft/weather damage): verify they are addressed to the household, carry heavy boxes with two hands and fragile/perishable ones upright, and place them in the package spot unopened, with perishables flagged.
success: All household-addressed packages inside at the package spot, unopened, upright per labels; misdelivered packages set aside and reported; perishables flagged/put in fridge per rule.
wrong: Brings in a neighbor's misdelivered package without noting it.
Opens packages.
Carries a 'this side up' box upside down.
fidelity: G: box carry mass and orientation
notes: Package-handling family (Entryway, Packages sections).

interpretation: Reorganize the shed into zones: long-handled tools hung on wall hooks, heavy items (soil bags, mower) low near the door, frequently used garden tools within reach, chemicals (pesticide, fertilizer, pool chlorine) high or locked and separated by compatibility, fuel cans away from ignition and heat. Nothing is discarded without approval and a clear walking path remains.
success: Every item sits in a zone that satisfies the rules: heavy items below height H, chemicals above child reach with incompatible ones (chlorine vs acid/fertilizer) separated, fuel away from ignition sources; long tools hung; clear path at least width W from door to back wall; item-location map updated; no item discarded without approval.
wrong: Shelves pool chlorine beside pool acid or fertilizer
Puts heavy soil bags on a high shelf
Throws out old-looking pots and tools without asking
fidelity: G: shelf load/height placement and clear-path width; S: chemical compatibility
user_sim: Hidden: preferred zone layout and which old items are keep vs discard. Necessary: 'Keep or toss the cracked pots?' before discarding. Unnecessary: asking whether chemicals should go up high (that is a rule).
notes: Same wording in 'Seasonal spring tasks' (bring spring tools forward) and 'Monthly / occasional reset'. Shared organize.zone skill with garage and closets.

interpretation: Organize the pool's flotation devices: approved life jackets sorted by size/weight rating and hung where they're easy to grab, children's sizes separated, noodles and toys in their bin, and the ring buoy and reaching pole left mounted and unobstructed at their rescue stations. Damaged devices are set aside and reported.
success: Life jackets grouped by size rating and hung in the designated spot; children's sizes reachable and separated; ring buoy and reaching pole on their stations, unobstructed, rope coiled ready; damaged items in a 'report' set and reported; toys separated from safety gear.
wrong: Packs the ring buoy and reaching pole into the shed with the toys
Mixes adult and child life jackets so sizes are hard to find
Puts a torn life jacket back into service
protect: rescue equipment unavailable in an emergency
fidelity: S: category/size grouping and rescue-equipment accessibility
notes: Rescue equipment must stay deployed, which is the key difference from organizing toys.

interpretation: Keep the bin area organized as a standing duty: each cart on its marked spot with labels and lids facing out, lids closed and animal latches set, spare liners and bin-cleaning supplies stocked where they belong, a clear path from the house to the carts and down to the curb, nothing stacked on the lids, and no litter.
success: At every periodic check: each cart at its marked position and orientation, lids closed and latched, path clear at width W, supplies at par, no litter; state recovers after injected perturbations (wind moves a cart, a visitor leaves a box on a lid).
wrong: Tidies once and ignores a cart blown over later
Stacks a box of recycling on top of a lid
Lets the liner stock run out without reporting
fidelity: S: zone/orientation states over time; G: path clearance
notes: 'Keep' marks a standing order evaluated across a multi-day episode.

interpretation: Reduce visible clutter in the specified room: return misplaced items to their home locations (including homes in other rooms), group the remaining loose items, clear surfaces and floor, bin obvious trash, and set aside unknown or possibly discardable items for the owner to decide rather than throwing them out; respect other residents' belongings and privacy zones.
success: Surface and floor clutter score below threshold; items with known homes at those homes (snapshot diff); unknown items in the set-aside bin with a summary to the owner; zero owned items discarded; intentional decor unchanged; private zones untouched.
wrong: Shoves clutter into closets and drawers (hidden, not homed)
Throws away papers and a child's artwork as clutter
Rearranges another resident's desk
fidelity: S: item home locations and ownership; G: surface clearance
compound: collect loose items from surfaces and floor
return items with known homes (including cross-room)
group unknown items in a set-aside bin
ask the owner about discard/donate candidates
user_sim: Hidden: what counts as clutter vs intentional display, who owns each item, and which items the owner wants gone. Necessary: asking about discarding specific items or about unowned unknowns. Unnecessary: asking whether the TV remote goes back to the TV caddy.
notes: Compound routine; the evaluator penalizes hidden-not-homed items.

interpretation: Gather objects of the same category scattered around the specified area (batteries, pens, chargers, spices, hair ties) into one group or container per category, at a granularity that suits the area (pens vs markers in an office), and without grouping items that must stay apart (chemicals with food, medications with candy).
success: Each category's items co-located in one zone or container (category purity at or above threshold, scatter count zero); no hazardous cross-grouping (chemicals with food, medication with candy).
wrong: Groups by color or size rather than function
Puts cleaning sprays in the same bin as snacks
Leaves several stray members of a category behind
fidelity: S: category assignment and co-location
user_sim: Hidden: the resident's category scheme when granularity is ambiguous (all writing tools together vs separate). Asking is necessary only if the area has no existing scheme; unnecessary for obvious categories.
notes: Basic organization primitive reused by many 'Organize X' entries.

interpretation: Design and set up storage zones for a space (pantry, garage, closet, kids' room): give each category a zone by frequency of use (prime reach zone), weight (heavy low), user (children's items at child height, hazards out of child reach) and nearness to where things are used (pans near the stove); mark the zones, move the items and record them in the item-location map.
success: Every category assigned to exactly one zone; zones satisfy the constraints (heavy below H, hazards above child reach, high-frequency items in the primary user's reach envelope, adjacency to point of use); items moved to their zones; map updated; shelf capacities respected.
wrong: Puts heavy items on top shelves
Places cleaning chemicals in the children's reach zone
Assigns zones by appearance, ignoring use frequency
protect: items unreachable for the main user
fidelity: G: zone geometry vs reach envelopes and shelf capacity
user_sim: Hidden: primary user and usage patterns. Necessary question when several residents share the space and logs don't show who uses it; unnecessary when usage logs are clear.
notes: Feeds 'Label storage'.

interpretation: Label bins, shelves and drawers with what is actually in them (verify after zoning): consistent names, readable size, facing outward, picture labels for pre-readers in children's areas, in the household's language, and removable labels on finished wood or rental fixtures.
success: Every target container has one label whose text matches its content category (verified against contents), visible from the normal access direction; picture labels in children's zones; no permanent adhesive on finished wood or rental surfaces.
wrong: Labels bins from the plan without checking what's inside
Sticks labels on the hidden side or upside down
Uses permanent adhesive labels on an antique dresser
fidelity: S: label-content match; G: label orientation and visibility
user_sim: Hidden: the household's naming preferences and language. Asking is necessary only when no existing labels set a convention.
notes: Follows 'Create storage zones'. Labels are verified against actual contents, so pre-printing labels from the plan fails when the bins differ.

text: Put frequently used items within reach.
interpretation: Rearrange things so the items a specific resident uses most are in that person's comfortable reach zone (roughly between hip and shoulder height, at the front of the shelf), allowing for a wheelchair user, an elderly resident who shouldn't climb, or a child, based on usage logs; less-used items move higher or lower, and hazardous items are never brought within a young child's reach.
success: The top-k most-used items for the target resident are inside that resident's reach envelope (no stool needed); displaced items relocated, not lost; hazards outside the child envelope; map updated and the resident told where things moved.
wrong: Uses a generic adult reach height for a wheelchair user
Moves cleaning products down to the toddler's reach while freeing space
Moves everything without telling the resident where it went
fidelity: G: per-person reach envelope vs shelf heights
user_sim: Hidden: who the items are for and which are 'frequently used' when logs are thin. Necessary question when several residents share the space; unnecessary when the command names the person and logs exist.
notes: Accessibility-driven organization.

text: Put infrequently used items into storage.
interpretation: Move rarely used items (seasonal decor, holiday dishes, off-season clothes, specialty appliances) from prime space to long-term storage (attic, basement, high garage shelves) in labeled bins, wrapping fragile items and putting heavy ones low; never put away things that must stay accessible (emergency kit, fire extinguisher, regular medication, documents needed soon).
success: Items with usage below threshold in long-term storage, in labeled bins whose labels match their contents; fragile items wrapped (no breakage); must-stay-accessible items still in their accessible spots; map updated.
wrong: Packs the emergency kit or fire extinguisher away in the attic
Stacks heavy dish boxes on top of fragile decor
Stores items in unlabeled bins
fidelity: S: usage classification and storage rules; G: bin stacking
user_sim: Hidden: which items the resident considers infrequent (e.g. a bread machine used every Sunday). Asking about borderline items is necessary; asking about obvious seasonal decor out of season is unnecessary.
notes: Season is a variation axis that flips which items count as infrequent.

interpretation: Sort a designated set of items (a closet, a box) into keep, donate and discard piles according to the owner's decisions and stated criteria: stained or broken items are discards, not donations; things charities won't take (recalled or expired car seats and cribs, used underwear) are excluded; sentimental or valuable items are never discarded without the owner's explicit OK. The robot proposes, the owner decides.
success: Every item in the pile matching the owner's hidden decision (or the stated criteria where the owner delegated); donate pile contains only acceptable items; no sentimental or valuable item in donate or discard without explicit approval; ambiguous items queried.
wrong: Puts a stained shirt and an expired car seat in the donate pile
Discards the photo album because it looked old
Sorts another resident's things without their approval
fidelity: S: per-item disposition labels with approval gating
user_sim: Hidden: the owner's decision per item. Necessary: asking about sentimental, valuable or ambiguous items, and confirming the discard batch once. Unnecessary: asking per item about obviously broken junk when the owner said 'toss anything broken'.
notes: Approval gate: discard and donate require the owner; a batch confirmation is acceptable.

interpretation: Gather the items approved for donation into one staging spot (by the door or in the garage), kept separate from the trash and keep piles; check each meets donation standards (clean, working, complete, not recalled or expired), empty pockets and drawers of donated clothing and furniture of personal items and papers, and include nothing that wasn't approved.
success: Only approved items in the donation pile, at the staging spot and physically separated from trash; pockets and drawers emptied, with found personal items returned to the owner; unacceptable items moved out and reported.
wrong: Adds unapproved items 'that seemed unused'
Leaves a passport or cash in a donated jacket pocket
Stages donations next to the trash bags so they get thrown out
fidelity: S: approval and acceptability states; staging location
notes: Follows 'Sort keep/donate/discard items'.

interpretation: Pack donated clothing, linens and soft goods into bags: clean, dry and folded, shoes paired (tied or banded), grouped by category, each bag tied and under the weight limit, and clearly labeled 'donation' so it isn't mistaken for trash, following the charity's requirements.
success: All approved soft goods bagged clean, dry and folded; shoes bound in pairs; each bag tied, under the weight limit and labeled 'donation'; no unapproved items included.
wrong: Uses unlabeled black trash bags, so the donations get thrown out
Bags damp clothes, which mildew
Bags shoes singly so pairs get separated
fidelity: S: bag contents, labels and textile states
notes: Soft-goods counterpart of 'Box donations'.

interpretation: Pack hard donation goods (dishes, books, toys, small appliances) into boxes: fragile items wrapped individually, heavy items such as books in small boxes, every box under the weight limit, small parts bagged with their item, cords secured to appliances, boxes taped and labeled with their contents and 'donation'.
success: All approved hard goods boxed; fragile items wrapped with zero breakage after a simulated handling shake; each box under the mass limit; parts kept with their items; boxes closed and labeled.
wrong: Packs heavy books into one huge box that can't be lifted
Stacks plates unwrapped, so they break
Separates a toy's pieces from the toy
fidelity: G: box packing geometry and mass limits
notes: Shares packing skills with the moving and travel packing entries.

interpretation: Count and record every pantry item: name, quantity (including partial levels in opened packages), unit, location, best-by/expiry date and opened status; flag expired, damaged (bulging or deeply dented cans, pantry moths) and duplicate items; put everything back where it was after counting.
success: Recorded inventory matches ground truth (counts exact, partial levels within tolerance, dates correct); expired, damaged, pest and duplicate flags correct; item poses restored (snapshot diff within tolerance); nothing discarded without approval.
wrong: Counts packages but ignores partial levels and dates
Throws away expired items without asking
Leaves the pantry rearranged after counting
fidelity: S: item records vs ground truth
notes: Inventory family; 'Check pantry before shopping' reuses the record.

interpretation: Record the refrigerator's contents (leftovers with their dates, condiment levels, produce freshness) while keeping door-open time short to protect the cold chain (scan in batches, closing the door in between); flag spoiled or expired items and leftovers past their safe days without throwing them out, and put items back where they were.
success: Record matches ground truth within tolerances; spoiled/expired flags correct; total door-open time under budget and fridge temperature never above the safe threshold; positions restored; nothing discarded without approval.
wrong: Holds the door open for the whole count, so the fridge warms up
Throws out leftovers it judged old without asking
Misses the moldy items at the back
protect: food warming into the danger zone
fidelity: S: records; P-lite: fridge air temperature rise vs door-open time
notes: Door-open thermal budget is the physical constraint.

interpretation: Record the freezer's contents, including unlabeled frosted packages (identify and label them), dates frozen and freezer burn, with minimal door-open time so nothing starts thawing; for a chest freezer, lift the baskets out and put the layers back in order.
success: Record matches ground truth; unlabeled packages identified (or marked unknown) and labeled; door-open time under budget with no item crossing the thaw threshold; chest-freezer layer order restored.
wrong: Leaves the chest freezer open while sorting everything onto the counter, partly thawing it
Guesses contents of unlabeled packages without checking
Repacks the chest freezer in a different order so old items get buried
fidelity: P: item thaw temperature vs time out of freezer; S: records
notes: Freezer counterpart of 'Inventory refrigerator'.

interpretation: Count cleaning products and tools: product, fill level (estimate partially used sprays by weight), location and tool condition (worn sponges, vacuum bags and filters, mop heads); keep containers closed and upright, never consolidate or mix partly used products, flag leaking or unlabeled containers, and re-latch the child lock afterwards.
success: Record matches ground truth (fill levels within tolerance); worn tools flagged; leaking and unlabeled containers flagged and isolated; no chemicals combined; containers upright and closed; child lock engaged at the end.
wrong: Pours two half-empty products together to save space
Leaves the cabinet's child lock open
Ignores an unlabeled bottle instead of flagging it
fidelity: S: records and chemical safety rules
notes: Feeds 'Check cleaning supplies' and 'Build household supply list'.

interpretation: Count shared and backstock toiletries (toilet paper, soap, shampoo, toothpaste, razors, menstrual products) in the bathroom cabinets and linen closet; note per-resident items only as far as the household allows, and don't open residents' private kits, drawers or medications; flag items that are running low.
success: Shared/backstock counts match ground truth; low flags correct; zero opening events on private kits, drawers or medication containers; nothing moved from residents' personal spaces.
wrong: Opens a resident's toiletry bag or medicine drawer to count
Counts a guest's personal products as household stock
Misses that toilet-paper backstock is low
fidelity: S: records with privacy constraints
notes: Privacy zones limit what may be inventoried.

interpretation: Inventory laundry supplies: detergent (estimate loads left from fill level and dose), pods, softener, dryer sheets, stain remover, bleach, hangers; note whether the detergent is HE-compatible with the washer, and flag pods stored within a child's reach.
success: Record matches ground truth; loads-remaining estimate within tolerance; HE mismatch flagged if present; pods within child reach flagged and moved up; low items flagged.
wrong: Counts bottles without estimating how many loads remain
Leaves detergent pods on a low shelf in a home with a toddler
Misses that the detergent isn't HE for an HE washer
fidelity: S: records and consumption estimates
notes: Inventory family; loads-remaining comes from volume and dose, which ties into the laundry module's detergent model.

interpretation: Inventory pet supplies per pet: food (days remaining at the current feeding rate), treats, litter, poop bags, flea/tick and prescription medication (next-dose dates and expiry), and toys and leashes; keep each pet's special items (such as a prescription diet for one cat) separate.
success: Per-pet record matches ground truth; days-remaining estimates within tolerance; expired or soon-due medications flagged; prescription diet tied to the right pet; low items flagged.
wrong: Lumps all pet food together, ignoring the prescription diet
Reports bag counts without days remaining
Misses an expired flea treatment
fidelity: S: per-pet records and consumption-rate estimates
notes: Feeds 'Check pet supplies'.

interpretation: Inventory office supplies: paper, ink/toner levels (read from the printer), pens (test for dried-out ones), stamps, envelopes, staples, tape and batteries; flag low items, and list dried-out pens for the resident rather than throwing them out.
success: Record matches ground truth; ink levels read from printer state; dried-out pens identified by test and flagged; low items flagged; desk items returned to place.
wrong: Guesses ink level from cartridge count
Throws away pens without testing or asking
Rummages through private papers on the desk
fidelity: S: records with device-state queries
notes: Inventory family; ink level is device state queried through the electrical module, not visual.

interpretation: List the tools present against what is expected (toolbox manifest, previous inventory), with condition (dull blades, broken handles, rust) and the charge state of battery packs; locate missing tools from the who-moved-what log; don't leave power tools plugged in or batteries on chargers; return each tool to its place.
success: Record lists present, missing (with last-seen location) and damaged tools correctly; battery charge states recorded; no power tool left plugged in; tools back at home positions.
wrong: Reports missing tools without checking the location log
Leaves the drill plugged in or a battery on the charger indefinitely
Doesn't note the rusted, unsafe tool
fidelity: S: manifest diff and condition records
notes: Inventory family; missing tools are found through the who-moved-what log.

interpretation: Refill point-of-use stock from household backstock: toilet paper in each bathroom, paper towels, hand-soap dispensers (refilled from bulk without overflowing or mixing soap types), tissues, trash liners, dishwasher pods; use the oldest backstock first, update the inventory, and add depleted backstock to the shopping list.
success: Every point-of-use location at or above par; dispensers refilled below the overflow line with the same soap type; oldest backstock used first; inventory decremented; depleted backstock on the shopping list.
wrong: Overfills the soap dispenser so it runs over the sink
Refills with dish soap instead of hand soap
Uses up the last backstock without adding it to the list
fidelity: S: par levels; liquid refill volume vs overflow as a scalar
notes: Ties the inventory layer to the shopping list.

interpretation: Proactively find consumables below their reorder threshold across the house, including partly used items whose level has to be estimated (a nearly empty shampoo, the last roll), taking consumption rate and lead time into account, and report them or add them to the list; no false alarms for items with enough backstock elsewhere.
success: Low-stock set reported equals ground truth (precision and recall at or above targets), accounting for backstock and consumption rate.
wrong: Flags dish soap as low although two spare bottles are in the pantry
Misses the nearly empty shampoo because the bottle is still present
Reports only items that are completely out
fidelity: S: level estimates and threshold logic
notes: Same family as 'Identify depleted items' (Shopping section).

interpretation: Compile a shopping list from detected low and depleted items, ingredients missing for planned meals and residents' requests, with quantities, preferred brands and sizes, dietary restrictions and allergies respected, grouped by store section, and with no duplicates of items already in stock.
success: List contains every needed item (recall at or above target) with correct quantities and brands, no item already sufficiently stocked, no allergen-violating item; grouped by section.
wrong: Adds peanut snacks despite a child's peanut allergy
Lists items already in the pantry
Leaves out the ingredients for the planned meals
fidelity: S: list composition vs household state
user_sim: Hidden: brand and size preferences and budget. Necessary to ask about a new item type with no purchase history; unnecessary to ask whether to add milk when it's out and bought weekly.
notes: Generic list builder; 'Build grocery list' and 'Build household supply list' (Shopping section) are its specializations.

interpretation: Update the existing shared shopping list with new information: add newly depleted items or a resident's spoken request, merge duplicates (summing quantities), remove items found in stock or already bought, and edit quantities, keeping other people's entries intact and asking when edits conflict.
success: List diff matches expected edits exactly: requested additions present, duplicates merged, stocked items removed, others' entries unchanged; conflicting edits (one adult adds an item, another removes it) resolved by a question; a child's candy request handled per household rule.
wrong: Overwrites the list with only the new items
Adds a duplicate line instead of merging
Silently deletes another resident's entry
fidelity: S: list state diff
user_sim: Hidden: which of two conflicting instructions wins (by authority or recency). Asking is necessary when two adults conflict; unnecessary for a simple addition.
notes: Tests the conflicting-instructions and authority features of the people layer on a shared artifact.

interpretation: Mark list items as done only when they have actually been obtained or put away (checked against bags, receipt or pantry), handling partial fulfillment (bought 1 of 3, so update the quantity), substitutions (noted) and items not found (left on the list).
success: List state matches ground truth of purchases: bought items crossed off, partial quantities updated, substitutions annotated, unbought items still open; history retained (marked, not deleted).
wrong: Crosses off everything after a shopping trip
Crosses off items that were out of stock
Deletes lines instead of marking them, losing history
fidelity: S: list item states vs purchase records
notes: Pairs with 'Unpack purchases'; the receipt is the evidence source, so crossing off unpurchased items is detectable.

interpretation: Unpack shopping bags or delivery boxes: cold and frozen items first, fragile ones (eggs, glass jars) carefully, check items against the receipt or order (report anything missing, damaged or wrong), leave items meant for particular people (prescriptions, gift-wrapped items) unopened, keep receipts, fold reusable bags and recycle the packaging.
success: All items out of bags with cold and frozen items unpacked first (time out of cold under limit); zero breakage; discrepancy report matches seeded missing/damaged/wrong items; personal and gift packages unopened and set aside for the recipient; receipt kept; bags folded and stored.
wrong: Unpacks dry goods first while ice cream melts
Opens a package addressed to a resident (a gift or prescription)
Throws away the receipt needed for a return
fidelity: S: ordering, discrepancy detection and privacy; G for fragile handling
notes: Followed by 'Put purchases away'.

interpretation: Put all purchases (groceries and non-food: toiletries, cleaning products, batteries, clothes) in their home locations: frozen and refrigerated first, new items behind older ones, chemicals away from food, a sensible new home for any new item type (then tell the resident where), and update the inventory.
success: Every purchased item at its home location (or a reasonable new home that was then announced); cold-chain limits met; FIFO order on shelves; no chemicals stored with food; inventory and map updated.
wrong: Puts the bleach in the pantry next to the cereal
Puts new milk in front of the old
Stashes new item types somewhere random without telling anyone
fidelity: G: shelf placement and FIFO depth order
user_sim: Hidden: preferred home for new item types. Telling the resident is required; asking beforehand is only necessary if several plausible homes conflict with house rules.
notes: Broader than 'Put groceries away' (Kitchen and Shopping sections), which is food-only.

interpretation: Collect appliance and device manuals and store them in the designated file or binder by room or category, matched to items the household actually owns (by model number); manuals for items no longer owned are set aside for the resident to decide, not discarded; note where digital copies exist.
success: Every manual for an owned item filed under the correct category and retrievable by appliance; obsolete manuals in the set-aside bin with the owner informed; none discarded.
wrong: Files manuals by guessing from the cover photo, mismatching models
Throws away manuals for appliances it thinks are gone
Leaves manuals scattered in different drawers
fidelity: S: document-appliance matching and filing
notes: Document family with 'Organize warranties' and 'Store receipts'.

interpretation: File warranty cards and documents together with their proof of purchase, organized by product and expiry date; record coverage end dates so they can be found when an appliance fails, and flag expired warranties for possible removal only with approval.
success: Each warranty paired with its receipt and filed by product; expiry dates recorded correctly; expired ones flagged and kept pending approval; retrieval query ('Is the fridge still under warranty?') answered correctly from the filing.
wrong: Files warranties apart from their receipts, so they can't be claimed
Throws out expired warranties without asking
Records the purchase date as the expiry date
fidelity: S: document pairing and date tracking
notes: Document family with 'Store manuals' and 'Store receipts'; evaluated partly by a retrieval query afterwards.

interpretation: Store receipts according to the household system: receipts still inside a return window in an accessible folder, tax, expense and warranty receipts filed by category and date, fading thermal receipts kept away from heat and light (or scanned), and trivial receipts discarded only where the household rule allows; receipts showing card details never left lying out.
success: Each receipt in the correct folder by category and date; return-window receipts retrievable; thermal receipts protected or scanned; disposal only per rule (shredding where card details show); no receipts left on open surfaces.
wrong: Throws away a receipt still needed for a return
Leaves receipts with card digits on the counter
Files thermal receipts in a sunny window drawer where they fade
fidelity: S: classification and storage of documents
notes: Document family; return-window dates make some receipts time-critical.

interpretation: Organize the household's keys: car keys and fobs on their hooks, spare house keys labeled by which lock they open (confirmed by trying them in the lock, not guessed) and kept somewhere secure rather than visible from the entry, unknown keys set aside for the owner rather than thrown away, and keyrings kept intact.
success: Every key with a label matching the lock it actually opens (verified by fit test) or placed in the unknown set; spares stored in a secure place not visible from the door; residents' keyrings not taken apart; car fobs on hooks.
wrong: Labels keys by guess
Hangs the spare house keys on a hook visible through the front window
Throws out keys it can't identify
fidelity: S: key identity and locations
notes: Same wording in 'Entryway / mudroom'.

interpretation: Sort craft supplies (paints, markers, yarn, paper, glue, beads, scissors, hot glue gun) into labeled containers by type, capping paints and glue, testing dried-out markers (discarded only with approval), keeping sharp tools and small beads out of a toddler's reach, and leaving works in progress and children's art intact.
success: Supplies grouped by type in labeled containers; all paints and glues capped; small parts and sharps above toddler reach; hot glue gun unplugged and stored; works in progress and artwork untouched; dried markers flagged.
wrong: Takes apart an unfinished project to sort its pieces
Puts the beads in an open bin on the floor where a toddler plays
Throws away children's drawings as scrap paper
fidelity: S: categories, work-in-progress flags and child-reach rules
notes: Child-safety reach rules shared with 'Organize toys'.

interpretation: Sort toys into bins by type or set (building bricks, puzzles with all their pieces, dolls, vehicles), keeping sets complete, placing them by age (an older sibling's small-part toys out of the toddler's reach), favorites easy to reach, broken toys flagged, and the child's display preferences respected; no toys discarded without a parent's approval.

wrong: Mixes pieces from different puzzles and games
Puts small-part toys in the toddler's low bin
Takes apart the child's Lego build to sort the bricks

user_sim: Hidden: the child's favorites and which builds are on purpose. Asking the child or a parent before disassembling a build is necessary; asking where puzzles go when the bins are labeled is unnecessary.

interpretation: Shelve the household's books using its scheme (genre, author, size or color), upright and spine-out with bookends, heavy books on lower shelves, keeping bookmarks in place, separating library books by due date, and leaving current reads out where they were.
success: Books ordered per the household scheme (order metric at or above threshold), upright with no leaning stacks, bookmarks still at their pages, library books grouped with due dates noted, current reads left in place.
wrong: Shelves the book someone is halfway through and loses its bookmark
Uses its own scheme (by color) when the household sorts by author
Mixes library books into the home collection
fidelity: G: shelf fit and upright stability; S: order scheme
user_sim: Hidden: the sort scheme. Necessary only when no consistent existing order can be inferred; unnecessary when the shelf already shows a clear scheme.
notes: Same wording in 'Bedrooms', 'Living room / family room' and 'Child-related household assistance'.

interpretation: Organize physical media (DVDs and Blu-rays, video games, CDs, vinyl records): every disc in its matching case (check), sorted by type and then by title or the household scheme, games by platform, vinyl stored upright (never stacked flat, which warps it) away from heat and sun, scratched discs flagged; discs handled by the edges.
success: Every loose disc in its matching case; media sorted per scheme; vinyl upright away from heat or sun sources; no new scratch or fingerprint events on disc surfaces; scratched discs flagged.
wrong: Puts discs into whichever empty case is nearest
Stacks vinyl records flat on top of each other
Grips discs across the data side

interpretation: Organize sports equipment (balls, bats, rackets, helmets, pads, bikes, weights, camping gear) by sport and owner in bins and on wall racks: heavy weights low, sweaty or wet gear dried before storing, under-inflated balls noted, helmets checked for cracks (flag them), ice-skate blades guarded.
success: Gear grouped by sport and owner; weights on the floor or low shelves; no wet gear in closed bins; damaged helmets flagged; skates guarded; walkway clear.
wrong: Puts dumbbells on a high shelf
Seals sweaty pads in a closed bin
Returns a cracked helmet to service unflagged
fidelity: G: rack/shelf placement by mass; S: condition flags
notes: Same wording in 'Garage'.

interpretation: Find the household items that are used up or effectively gone, including empty containers put back on the shelf or in the fridge, the empty box left in the cupboard and the last roll used, and check whether backstock exists before calling an item depleted.
success: Depleted-item set reported equals ground truth: empty-but-present containers detected, items with backstock not flagged.
wrong: Counts the empty cereal box on the shelf as stock
Flags paper towels as depleted although six rolls are in the garage
Checks only the kitchen
fidelity: S: fill-state perception and backstock aggregation
notes: Close relative of 'Detect low supplies' (threshold vs fully gone).

interpretation: Build the week's grocery list from depleted and low staples, the meal plan's ingredients minus what's on hand, and residents' requests, respecting dietary constraints (allergen-free for an allergic child, a vegetarian member), with quantities scaled to household size and planned meals and preferred brands; nothing already stocked.
success: List covers the meal-plan gaps and staples (recall at or above target) with correctly scaled quantities; no allergen or diet violations; no already-stocked items; brands match preferences.
wrong: Lists a recipe's full ingredient amounts ignoring what's on hand
Adds an allergen-containing product
Ignores a resident's request
fidelity: S: list vs household state and meal plan
user_sim: Hidden: meal plan if not recorded, and brand preferences. Asking what meals are planned is necessary when no plan exists; asking about routine staples is unnecessary.
notes: Food-specific counterpart of 'Make a shopping list'.

interpretation: Build the non-food supply list (cleaning products, paper goods, toiletries, laundry, pet supplies, batteries, light bulbs, filters, trash liners) with exact specs captured: bulb base and type, HVAC filter size and rating, fridge filter model, liner size, battery size.
success: List contains all low or depleted supplies, each with correct specs (filter size, bulb base, liner size); no stocked items; quantities sensible for consumption rate.
wrong: Writes 'air filter' without its size
Lists the wrong bulb base for the fixture
Adds items with plenty of backstock
fidelity: S: spec capture and list composition
notes: Specs come from the world model (fixtures and appliances), so items must be read rather than guessed.

interpretation: Before a shopping trip, reconcile the draft list with the pantry: remove items that are actually in stock in sufficient quantity, adjust quantities for partly used items, add missing staples noticed along the way, and check dates so expired stock doesn't count as on hand.
success: Final list reflects pantry ground truth: no sufficiently stocked items, expired-only items still listed, newly noticed depleted staples added, quantities adjusted.
wrong: Removes an item from the list because an expired package exists
Doesn't check partial levels (a nearly empty flour bag counts as stocked)
Adds nothing despite empty staples
fidelity: S: list reconciliation vs pantry state
notes: Shares the pantry record with 'Inventory pantry'.

interpretation: Before shopping, check the refrigerator against the list: perishables still fresh and in sufficient quantity come off the list, spoiled or nearly expired ones don't count, leftovers that cover planned meals reduce what's needed, and the door is open only briefly.
success: List reflects fridge ground truth (fresh sufficient items removed, spoiled ones still listed, leftover-covered meals adjusted); door-open time under budget.
wrong: Counts the wilted lettuce as on hand
Keeps the door open throughout the check
Ignores leftovers that cover Tuesday's dinner
fidelity: S: freshness-aware reconciliation
notes: Shares the freshness model with 'Inventory refrigerator'.

interpretation: Before shopping, check the freezer: items that cover the meal plan come off the list, freezer-burned items don't count, and check there's enough free freezer space for the frozen items on the list (flag if not), with minimal door-open time.
success: List reflects freezer ground truth; space check correct (flag when planned frozen purchases exceed free volume); door-open time under budget.
wrong: Counts freezer-burned meat as usable stock
Doesn't notice there's no room for the planned bulk frozen purchase
Leaves the chest freezer open while checking
fidelity: G: free volume vs planned purchases; S: stock reconciliation
notes: Adds a capacity check that the pantry and fridge versions lack.

interpretation: Check the bathroom supplies (toilet paper, hand soap, toothpaste, shampoo, cotton swabs, cleaning wipes) in every bathroom and the backstock, flag what's low and add it to the list, without opening residents' private drawers, bags or medicine cabinets.
success: Low-supply set matches ground truth across all bathrooms plus backstock; list updated; zero accesses to private zones.
wrong: Checks only one bathroom
Opens residents' private drawers or the medicine cabinet
Adds toilet paper although there's backstock in the closet
fidelity: S: levels and privacy constraints
notes: Lighter, shopping-oriented version of 'Inventory toiletries'.

interpretation: Check cleaning supplies before shopping: estimate fill levels of the sprays and liquids in use, check backstock, sponges, mop pads and vacuum bags/filters, flag what's low and add exact products to the list; re-latch the child lock afterwards.
success: Low and worn items correctly identified and listed with exact product types; no false alarms; child lock engaged at the end.
wrong: Reports a full-looking but nearly empty opaque spray as fine
Leaves the cabinet child lock open
Lists generic 'vacuum bags' without the model type
fidelity: S: levels, wear and safety state
notes: Shopping-oriented version of 'Inventory cleaning supplies'.

interpretation: Check the pet supplies before shopping: days of food left per pet at the current feeding rate, litter, poop bags, treats, and medications due soon or expired, adding needs to the list with exact products (the prescription diet, the right size of flea treatment).
success: Items whose days remaining are below the lead-time threshold are listed with exact product specs per pet; due or expired medications flagged; no false alarms.
wrong: Lists generic cat food for a cat on a prescription diet
Misses that food runs out before the next shopping day
Lists the wrong weight class of flea treatment
fidelity: S: per-pet consumption estimates
notes: Shopping-oriented version of 'Inventory pet supplies'.

interpretation: Gather the household's reusable shopping bags (from hooks, the closet, the car trunk, bags folded inside other bags), including insulated bags for cold items; check they're clean (wash or wipe any with leaked raw-meat juice); make sure there are enough for the size of the list, and put them by the exit or in the car before the trip.
success: Bag count at or above the estimate for the list volume (including insulated bags when frozen or cold items are listed); contaminated bags cleaned; bags staged at the exit or in the car before departure.
wrong: Brings two bags for a big weekly shop
Packs a bag with dried raw-chicken juice
Forgets the insulated bag when ice cream is on the list
fidelity: S: bag count and cleanliness states
notes: Pre-trip routine step; bag count estimate comes from list volume.

interpretation: Replenishment round: check every dispenser in the house (hand-soap pumps at each sink, dish-soap pump, foaming soap, hand sanitizer, lotion pump) and top up any below its refill threshold from the matching bulk refill in the stock cupboard. A missing refill goes on the shopping list. The robot does not substitute a different product.
conditional: Implicit per-dispenser branch: below threshold -> refill with the product class on its tag (foaming pump gets foaming refill or the house's dilution ratio); at or above threshold -> leave it untouched; matching refill out of stock -> add it to the shopping list and do NOT fill with a different product. Scenarios randomize fill levels and stock so a policy that refills everything, or never checks stock, fails.
success: Every dispenser that started below threshold is 80-100% full with its tagged product class and its pump primes on press. Dispensers that started adequate have the same level and product as before. No dispenser overflowed, counters have no soap residue, refill bottles are capped and back in stock with their level reduced by the transferred volume, and every exhausted product is on the shopping list.
wrong: Fills a hand-soap pump with dish soap or an all-purpose cleaner because the right refill was out
Tops up the foaming dispenser with undiluted liquid soap, so the foaming pump clogs
Refills only the kitchen dispenser and skips the bathroom and guest-bath dispensers
protect: no soap spilled on the floor (slip hazard)
no product mixing in a dispenser
refill bottles not left uncapped or contaminated
no overfilled dispenser leaking from the pump collar
fidelity: P: liquid volume transfer into a narrow neck (tilt, overflow, drip)
notes: Umbrella entry for the refill family in this section (soap, detergent, tissues, paper towels, toilet paper, trash bags, pet supplies). Shares the dispenser.refill skill with the bathroom and kitchen restock tasks.

interpretation: Restock soap at its points of use: liquid hand-soap pumps at every sink, the shower body-wash bottle, and bar-soap dishes. A dish holding a used-up sliver gets a fresh bar from stock, with the wrapper binned. Stock levels are updated afterwards.
conditional: Implicit: liquid pump below threshold -> refill with matching liquid; bar soap reduced to a sliver -> replace with a new bar (the sliver goes in the trash, or merges per house preference); bar or pump still adequate -> leave it. Out of stock -> shopping list, no substitution.
success: Every soap point below threshold is restocked: pumps 80-100% with hand soap, slivers replaced by a new bar sitting on a draining soap dish (not in standing water), wrappers in the trash, counters dry. Adequate points are unchanged, stock is decremented, and out-of-stock items are listed.
wrong: Puts the new bar on top of the mushy sliver in a dish full of water
Fills the hand-soap pump with shampoo or dish soap
Opens a new bar while the old one is still mostly full, wasting stock
protect: no soap pooled on the counter or tub edge
fidelity: P: liquid transfer volume and overflow at the pump neck
notes: Narrower sibling of T-92f2736b7f949c-01. The bathroom restock tasks in other sections share the soap.restock skill.

interpretation: Replenishment of detergents at their point of use. Laundry detergent goes to the washer shelf, decanting from a bulk jug or bag-in-box into the in-use dispenser or the washer's auto-dose reservoir. Dishwasher detergent (pods or powder) goes under the kitchen sink. Each refill matches the right product to the right appliance, and pods stay in a child-resistant closed container.
conditional: Implicit product branch: laundry reservoir/jug -> HE laundry detergent only; dishwasher -> dishwasher detergent only (never dish soap or laundry detergent); child or toddler in the household -> pods in a latched, high container. Low stock -> shopping list.
success: Laundry and dishwasher detergent supplies at point of use are above threshold with the correct product in each. The auto-dose reservoir is filled below its max line, pods sit in a closed, latched container out of child reach, no detergent is spilled, and stock and the shopping list are updated.
wrong: Puts liquid dish soap in the dishwasher dispenser, so the next cycle foams out onto the floor
Leaves the pod tub open on a low shelf in a home with a toddler
Overfills the washer's auto-dose reservoir past the max line
protect: no detergent pods reachable by children
no foam or flood event from the wrong product
no detergent spill on the laundry floor
fidelity: P: liquid volume transfer to reservoir max line
notes: Same wording appears in Laundry, where it means only the laundry dispenser. Here in replenishment it covers both detergent types and restocking from bulk storage.

interpretation: Restock tissues around the house (bedrooms, living room, bathrooms, office). Any empty tissue box is replaced with a new one from stock, slid into its decorative cover if it has one, with the perforated top opened and one tissue pulled up. The empty box goes to recycling.
conditional: Implicit: box empty (0 tissues) -> replace; box partially full -> leave in place; decorative cover present -> keep the cover and swap only the cardboard box inside. Stock exhausted -> shopping list.
success: Every location that had an empty box now holds a new opened box (inside its original decorative cover where one existed), with a tissue protruding. Partially full boxes are untouched, empty boxes are in recycling, and stock is decremented.
wrong: Puts a new box next to the empty one and leaves the empty box in place
Throws the decorative cover away with the empty cardboard box
Replaces partially full boxes, wasting stock and leaving several open boxes around
protect: decorative covers not damaged or discarded
no recyclable cardboard in the trash
fidelity: S
notes: Part of the refill family in Shopping and replenishment.

interpretation: Replace the empty paper-towel roll in the kitchen. The holder type is randomized: countertop spindle, under-cabinet bar with a spring-loaded arm, or wall dispenser. The new roll is mounted in the household's established orientation, the empty core goes to recycling, and a spare roll stays at the point of use if that is the house convention.
conditional: Implicit: roll empty or nearly empty -> replace; roll adequate -> leave it. The household orientation (sheet over the front vs under) follows the observed convention.
success: The holder carries a full roll, seated so it spins and tears cleanly, in the household orientation. The empty core is in recycling, stock is decremented, and no unrolled sheets are left trailing on the counter or floor.
wrong: Sets the new roll standing on the counter without mounting it
Mounts it reversed from the household convention
Snaps the under-cabinet spring arm by levering it
protect: holder arm not bent or broken
no wet counter soaking the new roll
fidelity: G: roll insertion onto spindle / spring-arm clearance
user_sim: Hidden: orientation preference (over/under) and whether a spare roll is kept on the holder. No question is needed when the previous roll's orientation was observable. Asking 'over or under?' is necessary only when no prior evidence exists and the resident has a recorded strong preference.
notes: Shares the roll-replacement skill with toilet paper (T-0017f0bf822016-01).

interpretation: Restock toilet paper in every bathroom, including the guest bath. Empty or near-empty rolls on spring-loaded spindles, open-arm holders or standing holders are replaced in the household's orientation, the spare-roll basket in each bathroom is topped up, and empty cores go to recycling. An occupied bathroom is not entered: the robot waits or comes back later.
conditional: Implicit: roll empty/near-empty -> replace; spare basket below N -> top up; bathroom occupied (door closed/locked, person inside) -> knock-and-wait or defer, never enter.
success: Every bathroom holder carries a usable roll in the house orientation, each spare basket holds at least N rolls, cores are recycled, and no roll touches a wet floor. The privacy log shows no entry into an occupied bathroom.
wrong: Leaves the new roll on the tank lid without mounting it
Flushes the empty core or the wrapper
Opens the door to an occupied bathroom to restock it
protect: no rolls soaked on the floor
no flushed cardboard causing a clog
fidelity: G: spring spindle compression and roll insertion
user_sim: Hidden: orientation preference; the guest bath may be in use by a visiting guest. A necessary 'May I come in to restock?' happens only when the bathroom is occupied and the task is urgent, otherwise the robot defers. Asking which bathrooms need it is unnecessary: it should check them all.
notes: Bathroom restock tasks elsewhere reuse the roll-replacement skill.

interpretation: Restock trash-bag supplies: each bin's spare-bag roll (kept in the bin bottom or an under-sink dispenser) has stock in the correct size. Kitchen bins take 13-gal drawstring, bathroom bins 4-gal, outdoor and garage bins 33-gal, and compost caddies take certified-compostable liners. Any bin standing empty without a liner gets a fresh one fitted over the rim.
conditional: Implicit size/stream branch: compost caddy -> compostable liner only; trash bin -> plastic liner of matching size; bin already lined -> do not double-line. Size out of stock -> shopping list, do not force a wrong size.
success: Every bin has exactly one liner of the correct size and stream, rim-tucked so it does not slide in. Each bin's spare-roll store holds stock, and the shopping list holds any size that ran out.
wrong: Puts a plastic trash bag in the compost caddy
Fits a 4-gal bag into the 13-gal kitchen bin so it slips in
Stacks several liners in one bin
protect: compost stream not contaminated with plastic
no liner slipping into the bin and spilling trash on next use
fidelity: G: liner opening vs bin rim circumference
notes: Liner skill shared with 'Take out trash' and 'Replace trash liner' tasks in the kitchen and cleaning sections.

interpretation: Restock pet supplies at their points of use. Kibble moves from the large bag into each pet's airtight bin, keeping the original bag inside the bin for the lot number. Poop-bag rolls go into the leash dispenser, cat litter into the bin by the box, treats into their jar. Each supply stays separated per pet, and lids stay latched so the dog cannot raid them.
conditional: Implicit per-pet branch: dog food -> dog bin, cat food -> cat bin, prescription-diet pet -> only its prescription food; supply below threshold -> refill, otherwise leave; supply out -> shopping list.
success: Each pet's food bin holds its own product above threshold with the lid latched, and the original bag (lot number) is retained. The poop-bag dispenser has a roll, the litter supply is restocked, and no kibble or litter is on the floor. The dog never gained access to an open bag during the episode.
wrong: Pours dog food into the cat's bin (or regular food into the prescription-diet bin)
Leaves the big kibble bag open on the floor where the dog eats from it
Dumps fresh kibble on top of old crumbs and discards the bag with the lot number
protect: no pet overeating from unsecured food
no litter dust cloud in living areas
fidelity: S
notes: Pairs with the pets-domain feeding tasks: restocking is inventory, portioning is feeding.

interpretation: Notice that a delivery has happened. Evidence can be a doorbell ring or knock, a courier seen on the doorbell camera, a package appearing on the porch, at the side door, in the mailbox or in the building mailroom/locker, or a carrier notification. Log it with time, location and count. Look-alikes must not count: a flyer, a solicitor ringing, or the household's own outgoing return waiting for pickup.
success: A delivery-event record exists within the time budget after each seeded drop, with correct location and package count. No record exists for flyers, solicitors or the outgoing package, and packages hidden behind a planter or at the side door are found.
wrong: Logs the household's own outgoing return in the pickup spot as a new delivery (and later brings it inside)
Only checks the front porch and misses the package left at the side door
Opens the front door to the solicitor who rang, treating any ring as a courier
protect: door not opened to unknown visitors
no false delivery alarms spamming residents
fidelity: S
notes: Fused heading in the source ('Package and delivery handling- Detect delivery.'), split at parse time. First step of the package pipeline T-e54aee68e3c2e0-01 .. T-9e2c8313a4b5e9-01.

interpretation: Read each package's shipping label and check the addressee name and street address against the household roster, including known nicknames and maiden names. A package for a neighbor or a former occupant is set aside unopened and an adult is told. A package for a household member goes to that person's area unopened.
conditional: Implicit: label matches household -> accept and route to the addressee; address mismatch (neighbor, wrong unit) -> do not open, keep separate, notify an adult; household address but unknown name (former occupant) -> hold and ask an adult.
success: Each package carries a verification status matching its seeded truth. Misdelivered packages are unopened in the hold area with an adult notified, and household packages are routed to the correct addressee.
wrong: Opens a neighbor's misdelivered package
Stacks the former occupant's package with household mail as if it were ours
Flags a resident's package as wrong because it uses their maiden name
protect: no opening of mail not addressed to the household
fidelity: S
user_sim: Hidden: aliases and former-occupant names. A necessary question: 'This box is for J. Ortiz at number 14, not us. Return it to the neighbor?' Asking about a package clearly addressed to a resident is unnecessary.

interpretation: Put incoming packages in the household's designated package area (entry bench, office corner, garage shelf, or per-recipient shelves), stacked heavy-below-light and out of walkways. A package labeled perishable or refrigerate (meal kit, medication cold-pack) is not left in a hot or freezing area: its recipient is told immediately.
conditional: Implicit: normal package -> designated area, per-recipient spot if the house has them; perishable/temperature-sensitive label -> notify the recipient at once and, only if pre-authorized, refrigerate the contents; no designated area known -> ask once rather than invent one.
success: Every package sits in the designated (and per-recipient, if defined) area. The stack is stable with no fragile box under a heavy one, walkways and doors are clear, and perishables were notified or refrigerated before exceeding their safe-temperature window.
wrong: Leaves the package in the hallway blocking the door path
Stacks a heavy box on one marked fragile
Leaves a meal kit in a 35 C garage for hours
fidelity: G: stack stability and walkway clearance
user_sim: Hidden: designated area and per-recipient spots. Necessary question only when no area is on record. Asking where each subsequent package goes once the area is known is unnecessary.

interpretation: Take all packing material out of an opened package: air pillows, bubble wrap, paper fill, packing peanuts, foam inserts, desiccant packets. Before anything is discarded, the fill is searched for small parts, hardware bags, manuals, receipts and gift cards, which stay with the item. Desiccant goes out of pet and child reach.
success: The item is free of packing and intact. Every seeded small part, manual and receipt is co-located with the item. All fill is collected (none on the floor) and sorted by stream, and desiccant is in a closed trash bin.

interpretation: Find: given a request for a specific item whose current location is hidden (e.g. 'find my reading glasses'), locate that exact instance using last-seen memory and likely-location priors, looking inside containers and under/behind occluders, and confirm it by pointing it out or bringing it as asked.

success: Robot's identity assignment for every probe object matches ground truth; indeterminate hazardous items are flagged rather than guessed; no unknown chemical opened, sniffed or mixed.

Identifies by color/shape alone and confuses bleach with vinegar
Forces a wrong charger into the device after misidentifying the connector

interpretation: Read: extract the needed information from printed, handwritten or displayed text — mail addressee, a note left on the counter, recipe quantities, appliance error codes, product labels with locale date formats — and act on exactly what it says, without reading other people's private documents.

interpretation: Sort: physically partition a mixed set of items into destination groups by a stated or household-standard criterion (laundry by color/fabric, recycling streams, mail by recipient, cutlery by type), placing every item in the correct bin.

wrong: Sorts by the wrong criterion (size instead of color)
Drops ambiguous items into arbitrary bins
Leaves part of the pile unsorted

interpretation: Categorize: assign each item to the correct semantic category in the household's scheme — junk mail vs bills vs personal, perishable vs shelf-stable, recycling vs trash vs compost, keep/donate/discard — including edge cases such as greasy pizza boxes, receipts and window envelopes containing checks.

Puts a greasy pizza box in recycling where local rules forbid it
Applies generic rules ignoring local ones (e.g. glass not accepted curbside)

interpretation: Unpack: take items out of a bag, box or suitcase and put each where it belongs — groceries with frozen and cold items first, travel clothes split into dirty (hamper) and clean (closet), a package checked against its packing slip — and deal with the packaging.

interpretation: Store: put an item into its proper storage place for its type, owner and condition — leftovers airtight, labeled and in the fridge; chemicals high or locked away from food and children; seasonal clothes in bins; valuables in the owner's place — so it is safe and can be found later.

interpretation: Retrieve: go and get a specified known item from where it is kept and bring it to the requester or place — 'bring me the scissors from the office drawer' — choosing the right instance, closing storage behind you, and carrying it safely (scissors closed, handle toward the person).

interpretation: Organize: impose or restore a logical system on a space's contents — group like items, give each a home, keep frequently used things accessible, label, respect the existing system and ownership — so things are findable and the space is usable; this goes beyond tidying surfaces.
success: Subsequent simulated-resident retrieval requests succeed faster than before; all items grouped; nothing discarded; owners' items remain in their zones; existing labels honored.

interpretation: Restock: bring a consumable at its point of use back to par from backstock — oldest stock first, the right product, no overfilling — or put it on the shopping list when backstock is short.

interpretation: Label: attach accurate, legible labels — contents and date on leftovers and freezer bags, bin contents, owner names, a decanted chemical's name and hazard — placed where they will be seen in storage and that stay attached in cold or damp conditions, in the household's format.

interpretation: Inventory: produce an accurate record of the items, quantities, locations, conditions and expiry dates in a scope (pantry, emergency kit, linen closet, tool chest) and compare it with the expected list to flag missing, low, duplicate and expired items.

Logs duplicates as a single item
Omits condition/expiry
